messages:
maria_cs: Hey team — I'm drafting a short customer-facing runbook for high-throughput onboarding customers (account health + renewal-risk focus). Need quick ops + eng input on streaming/batching/caching best-practices we can share with customers. TL;DR must be actionable and one-pager-ish.

ashley_pm: Love that. Can we make 3 sections: 1) Quick checks for Day 0 health, 2) Runtime knobs (batching/caching/streaming), 3) Signals to watch for renewal risk? Keep it checklist style.

maria_cs: Yes. Starting draft below — throwing to engineering for accuracy: 

--- RUNBOOK DRAFT (one-pager) ---
1) Day 0 health checklist (what CS does)
- Confirm model & version pinned in account config.
- Verify DNs & region routing (avoid cross-region fallbacks).
- Ensure live API keys rotated and alerts set.
- Run simple smoke test: single request -> streaming response -> < 800ms median.

2) Runtime knobs (customer-facing guidance)
- Edge priming / session pooling: recommend a small warm pool of N parallel sessions (default 3) to reduce cold-kv miss latency during bursts.
- Adaptive batching: enable client-side batching window 5–20ms for chat-heavy apps; server-side batch max_tokens set to 2048 for long contexts.
- Prefix caching: advise caching the last stable system prompt + common user prefixes in client to let us apply prefix-KV hits.
- Graceful degrade: configure fallback route to a lower-cost model (quantized) for non-critical paths.

3) Streaming best-practices
- Use token-streaming with small chunk size (default 64 tokens) and client-side assemble to show partial UX.
- Backpressure: if network spikes, pause stream and retry with exponential backoff; do not fall back to non-streaming synchronously.

4) Telemetry & renewal signals (what to capture)
- Engagement_rate: proportion of sessions with >= 2 prompts in 24h. Decline > 30% over 7d -> flag.
- Error_rate by route: if 5xx or 429 spikes > 2x baseline, open incident.
- Latency_p50/p95: p95 > target SLA + 150ms for 3 consecutive days -> CS outreach.
- Cost-per-successful-interaction metric: rising cost with flat usage -> discuss model/quantization.

5) Quick remediation playbooks (if things go wrong)
- If cold-start latency spikes: increase warm pool by 2x, enable prefix prefill for top 10 flows.
- If 429s during ramp: throttle client-side burst, increase dedicated capacity from Redwood Dedicated or enable burst pool.
- If quality regressions after model swap: rollback to pinned version, capture eval prompt set, escalate to ML team.

--- end draft ---

maria_cs: engineering, any wording or technical corrections? rlly trying to avoid deep jargon.

tomi_se: Nice. A few small clarifications:
- "warm pool of N parallel sessions" -> call out sessions = long-lived KV contexts, not OS sessions. Recommend default N=3 per tenant for mid-tier.
- "server-side batch max_tokens 2048" -> better say "configure max_batch_sequence_length" and include per-model caps. Keep as guideline.

kevin_eng: Add a short snippet for client-side backoff example: 
```
# pseudo backoff logic
delay = 100ms
for attempt in range(1,5):
  resp = call_streaming_api()
  if resp.ok: break
  sleep(delay)
  delay *= 2
```
Also mention jitter.

liam_sre: Ops notes to include for CS:
- Where to look in Console for token-level cost and latency breakdown (link).
- Quick query to run in observability: `filter route == \'/generate\' | stats p50(p95) by tenant`
- If alerting, set runbook to automatically create a high-sev ticket and call SRE.

maria_cs: Good. Ashley or Product: any callouts for renewal conversations?

ashley_pm: For renewal risk playbook add: 
- If Engagement_rate down and Cost-per-success up -> schedule 1:1 with customer and propose: prompt engineering consult, reduce sampling/temp, model switch to cheaper variant for non-critical flows.
- Provide a 4-point action plan in the outreach email: observations, impact (cost/latency), recommended quick fixes, offer a joint call.

maria_cs: Perfect. I'll iterate and publish a short customer-facing PDF + internal CS checklist. Final ask for wording: can Eng sign off on the 'default numbers' (pool=3, batch window 5–20ms, chunk=64)?

tomi_se: I sign off on defaults for mid-tier. For enterprise accounts we recommend pilot-specific tuning.

kevin_eng: +1. Add one line: "If you enable prefix caching, validate PII policies with Security."

deploy-bot: deployment: runbook-v1.0 published to /s3/runbooks/customer-success/edge-priming-runbook.pdf by deploy-bot at 2024-07-02T15:18:21Z :rocket:

maria_cs: Awesome — thanks everyone. I'll send the published link to customers in the next onboarding batch and include the short checklist in handoff docs. :pray:
